evidence.notes:
Import entry points (all go through reconcileRepository -> planImport -> planTransferHolds; importer.ts is the only writer of plan_revisions/runs/epics from tracked files, checked by grep of INSERT INTO plan_revisions/runs): (1) startup import, Workspace.openStore -> this.reconcile() (workspace.ts:271); (2) heartbeat auto-reconcile, safeReconcile -> reconcile() (workspace.ts:434); (3) the reconcileRepository command (commands/repository.ts:102), used by MCP reconcile_repository (mcp/tools/discovery.ts:83) and the desktop shell action (renderer shellActions.ts:246). A 'pull' is a git pull followed by (2) or (3). Profiles (profileImport) and branchEpics (read-only) do not import revisions or runs.

Design: conflict stored as kind='epic', entity=epicId so get_storage_status reports the epic id (a kind='run' row for a not-yet-local run would resolve epicId to the run id in storage.ts conflictsOf). No schema change. 'Newer' is implemented as 'a saved revision this DB lacks, or a pointer off the transferred revision': saving is refused locally while a transfer is open, so any unknown revision is a save from elsewhere; a pure number comparison let a same-number fork from another machine slip through and move current_revision_id (plan_revisions has no unique (epic_id, number)). Holding all of an epic's tracked changes (not only the revision) keeps one conflict per epic and one resolution; comments still import.

Red-team (reviewer subagent + self): found and fixed (a) local epic_state exports during a hold (ticket status change, epic status, transfer completion) overwrote the held current.json/state.json, cleared the conflict and silently lost the pulled revision -> exportEpic now refuses while hasTransferHold (finalizer.ts:185); (b) a matching read-back could complete the epic over held changes, after which a held run would import onto a completed epic -> assertStillTransferable refuses (transfers.ts:473); (c) same-number fork / pointer-move bypass (above); (d) stale conflict after a run-only hold + cancel -> prefix clear in storeConflicts. Checked and survived: other writers, re-detection every heartbeat (held files never marked synced), prefix clear cannot remove non-hold conflicts, deterministic message so problemsChanged does not spam events, epics.ts/renderer only display conflicts. Consciously not fixed: if the person changed the epic's state during a hold, after cancel the reconcile reports the existing pending-export conflict and the existing resolution (flush) writes local state over the pulled pointer; this is the pre-existing concurrent-edit semantics (see discovery), now visible rather than silent and documented in the runbook.

Keeping the stale parts after a final refusal would let the 'read back again from the start' that the guide prescribes merge into them, so an item since moved out of the project could still count as present. Non-final over-cap parts write nothing, so the earlier parts are kept, as the ticket asks. A part refused at the schema boundary (malformed or over 8,000,000 characters) changes nothing, final or not, same as the existing schema refusals; the runbook now says so. The non-final refusal message tells the agent to move extra items out, discard the read-back with start_transfer and a fresh idempotencyKey (which clears readback_json, checked at transfers.ts startTransfer), and read back from the start.

Red-team: (a) Bypass: readback_json has exactly one writer (acceptReadbackPart); every external entry runs the command schema through workspace parseInput, and the MCP tool uses the same part schema. (b) Fail-open: zod runs refinements even after continuable issues such as a list over its max or an unknown key. I checked that the size walk survives non-JSON values (bigint in an unknown key or in sortOrder): it counts them as null and does not throw, and another issue refuses those parts anyway. (c) Huge input: the walk stops once it passes the cap, so it never builds a 500 MB string. (d) Exactness: the boundary test uses quotes, backslashes, newlines, control characters, non-ASCII, surrogate pairs, null, 1e21, -0 and a missing optional key, and passes at exactly 8,000,000 characters and fails at one more. A mutation that ignored escapes failed it. (e) Dedupe: an item sent again does not count twice, which the at-limit resend in the it.each shows. (f) Vacuity: each new test was shown failing without its behavior (see checks).

Discoveries:
- title: Bound the accumulated read-back's serialized size, not only its item counts
  reason: The count caps times the per-field bounds still allow about 1,100 x 515k + 200 x 502k characters (~650M) in transfers.readback_json, above V8's maximum string length (~536M). toJson in acceptReadbackPart would then throw a RangeError, which surfaces as 'internal' (it fails closed, because the transaction rolls back). A faithful copy of a maximal packet is itself near that size (packet_json has the same exposure), so a byte cap on the total needs a decision about the largest supported plan.
  ticket: DM-312
- title: Cap request bytes at the MCP/IPC transport before JSON parsing
  reason: The 8,000,000-character part cap runs after the transport has received and parsed the whole request. An oversized submit_transfer_readback (or any tool call) is still read fully into memory by the stdio MCP server and the app before zod refuses it.
  ticket: DM-312
- title: Guide wording: a final part that is refused as malformed or over the size limit does not end the read-back
  reason: skills/linear-transfer.md section 7 says 'A final part always ends the read-back, whatever the result'. The runbook now spells out the exception: a schema refusal, which includes the new part-size cap, changes nothing. Schema refusals already behaved this way before DM-312. The guide was left unchanged to avoid a SKILLS_VERSION bump inside this ticket.
  ticket: DM-312

outputs.summary: Bounded the Linear read-back. New READBACK_LIMITS in src/core/schemas.ts next to LIMITS: partChars 8,000,000 (characters of JSON in one submitTransferReadback part), milestones 200, issues 1,100, relations 15,100 (each the packet-side limit LIMITS.sprints / LIMITS.tickets / LIMITS.edges+LIMITS.relations plus a fixed allowance of 100 unexpected items, READBACK_UNEXPECTED_ITEMS). (1) Per-part cap at the command boundary: linearReadbackPart = linearReadback.refine(...) is the readback field of COMMAND_SCHEMAS.submitTransferReadback (and of the submit_transfer_readback MCP tool, whose description now states the cap). It measures the exact JSON.stringify length without building the string (stops past the cap), so a part over 8,000,000 characters is refused with invalid_input at path readback before the service runs: nothing is merged or stored, final or not. (2) Merged caps in acceptReadbackPart: after mergeReadback (distinct items, re-sent items replace their copies), a NON-final part that would exceed a list limit is refused with invalid_input naming the limit (message 'A transfer read-back holds at most 1100 issues; with this part it would hold 1101. ...', details {limit, max, count}) before any write, so the stored parts and updated_at stay exactly as they were and no event is logged. A FINAL part past a limit keeps the DM-290/291 contract: its merge-and-clear commits in its own transaction (so it still ends the accumulation, as the guide promises), then it is refused with invalid_input. submitTransferReadback still has no idempotency key, no outer transaction, and its in-transaction guard is unchanged. linearReadback is no longer exported (its only outside user moved to linearReadbackPart; avoids a ts-prune finding). Runbook docs/runbooks/linear-transfer.md gains a 'Size limits' section with the four values and the refusal behavior. The guide skills/linear-transfer.md gives no page size ('Send it in parts when it is large'), so its paging advice cannot exceed the cap; it was left unchanged and SKILLS_VERSION was not bumped.

Detection rule (finalizer.ts unimportedHash): compute trackedEpicHash(current.json, state.json) on disk; the export may write only when the hash equals the sync_state exported_hash or imported_hash, or a hash in this machine's export intent. A file this machine wrote has the exported hash (recordExport stores the hash of the exact texts written), and the hash is CRLF-insensitive. The export intent (local/exports/<epicId>.json, machine-local) is written before any file is replaced and lists [new state over old pointer, both new], so a process killed before the commit still recognises its own write. A failed write also restores both files. If neither file exists, the export writes them as before, since there is nothing to lose.
